examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Limit at Infinity of a Power Function With an Odd Power
examples.worked_solution:
First, we note that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{{x}^{3}}{2} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{2}\cdot {x}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph $y=x^3$ is power function with an odd positive power and therefore has the property that

$$
\lim_{x\to-\infty } x^3 = -\infty.
$$

Multiplication by the positive constant $\dfrac{1}{2}$ does not affect the limit at infinity. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{3} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{3} \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

If the figure above shows the graph of $f(x),$ then

${lim}_{x\to \infty }({x}^{6}{(f(x))}^{1/5})=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
Applying the product rule and the root rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }({x}^{6}{(f(x))}^{1/5}) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }({x}^{6}\cdot \sqrt[5]{f(x)}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{6}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }\sqrt[5]{f(x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{6}\cdot \sqrt[5]{{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

From the graph, we get that ${lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x)=-32.$ Therefore, the above becomes:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }({x}^{6}{(f(x))}^{1/5}) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{6}\cdot \sqrt[5]{-32} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{6}\cdot (-2) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }-2{x}^{6} \\  & =-2\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{6}\end{aligned}
$$

The graph $y={x}^{6}$ looks similar to an upward parabola, so

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{6}=\infty .
$$

However, multiplying by the negative coefficient $-2$ causes $y=-2{x}^{6}$ to look more like a downward parabola. This changes the sign of the limit. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(-2{x}^{6})=-{lim}_{x\to \infty }({x}^{6})=-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
